diagnostic_evidence.quote: The localized CBS dynamics admit $\pi$ as a stationary distribution in the following~cases.
In the mean-field limit, our \emph{localized CBS} method was shown to have desirable properties such as affine-invariance and unbiased sampling from Gaussian distributions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion claim exact/unbiased Gaussian sampling. The formal result only proves that the Gaussian target is a stationary distribution for certain parameter choices; no convergence from arbitrary initial distributions or uniqueness of the stationary distribution is established. Thus the prose claims more than the formal content supports.

failure_location.quote: We prove that our algorithm is affine-invariant and exact for Gaussian distributions in the mean-field setting.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the abstract and conclusion to state that the Gaussian target is a stationary distribution, or add a convergence proof.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exactness/unbiasedness for Gaussian targets is not established; only stationarity is supported.
issues.title: Overclaim of exact Gaussian sampling from stationarity only
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening of an advertised guarantee, but it withdraws the exactness claim; no new global proof is supplied.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma states the equivalence for any α>0, but the formula λ=α'/(α-α') requires λ>0, hence α>α'. It also omits the parameter γ, while the proof uses γ=2α'/(α'+1). Without these conditions the localized CBS dynamics are not specified correctly and the claimed equivalence fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses α>α' and γ=2α'/(α'+1) to the lemma statement.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false or ill-posed for α≤α' and for any γ other than 2α'/(α'+1).
issues.title: Missing parameter conditions in Gaussian equivalence lemma
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local addition of missing parameter conditions and preserves the intended theoretical comparison.

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand side is the weighted mean μ_{β,κ C/β}, whose weights should be w_{β,κ C/β}. The right-hand side instead uses w_{α,λ C}, the weights for the covariance preconditioner. This does not approximate the intended mean; for an unweighted covariance preconditioner, α and λ are not even defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace w_{α,λ\widehat{\mathbf C}} by w_{\beta,\kappa\widehat{\mathbf C}/\beta} in the random-batch mean definition.
issues.overall_effect: The random-batch algorithm as written does not implement the localized CBS dynamics and is ill-defined for the default unweighted covariance.
issues.title: Random-batch mean uses covariance weights instead of mean weights
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local substitution of the correct weights; it restores the intended algorithm without changing its architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When we use random batching, we will choose relatively large values of $\nu$ (e.g., $\nu=0.5$)

issues.failure_explanation: For ν<1 there is positive probability that no j≠i satisfies θ_n^{i,j}≤ν, making the denominator zero. The algorithm does not specify how to handle this case, so the random-batch mean is not well-defined for all realizations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a fallback when the denominator is zero, e.g., use all other particles or set the mean to the current particle.
issues.overall_effect: The random-batch algorithm can fail to be well-defined on a set of positive probability.
issues.title: Random-batch mean denominator can vanish
issues.why_classification: A short local degenerate-case fix restores well-definedness without changing the method.
